caption: The model editor with client_demos\example_1\example_1.pyfds open (File > Open). The menu bar: File, Edit, Model, Devices, Output, Analysis (running FDS), Results, View, Tools, Help.
Project Explorer filter: typing TC_ leaves only the four thermocouples (and the groups that hold them). It also takes tag: and type: (for example type:vent).
The same filter with type:vent - every vent of the model, nothing else.
File menu.
Edit menu: Undo/Redo, clipboard, and the new Visibility and Transform submenus.
Model menu: the editors, the Add... commands, Add from Library, Model Checks, and (right column) Add Special, Open Mesh Boundaries and the Draw, HVAC, Scenarios and Floors submenus.
Devices menu.
Output menu.
Analysis menu (running FDS): Run Simulation, parallel/cluster/cloud runs, Open Smokeview After Run, Stop and Cancel, Monitor Simulation.
Results menu of the editor: Open PyFDS Results, View Results of Last Run, Open Smokeview... (any .smv in Smokeview) and Open Results Folder.
View menu: standard views, display options and the Rendering Mode submenu.
Tools menu, with the new Fire Engineering Calculators.
Help menu: the FDS User Guide and the Smokeview Verification Guide open in the PDF viewer.
Edit > Visibility: hide and show objects.
Edit > Transform: move, rotate, scale and mirror the selection.
Model > Add from Library: surfaces, fuels and materials from the library.
Model > Add Special: typed surfaces (burner, supply, exhaust), complex stoichiometry reactions, liquid fuels.
Model > Model Checks: every 'check my model' command in one place (some used to be under Tools).
View > Rendering Mode: wireframe, shaded, outlines, realistic.
Tools > Fire Engineering Calculators, 'Fire size and cell size' for example 1's 180 kW burner: the characteristic diameter D* = 0.48 m and the cell sizes for D*/dx from 10 to 20.

step: W5 calculator Fire size and cell size

caption: 'Heat detector response' for the same fire, the ceiling 2.25 m above the burner top and the detector on the fire axis. The calculator uses a standard sprinkler-type link (RTI 50, 68 C), not example 1's fast detector.
'Smoke filling time (NFPA 92)' for example 1's room (4.8 x 3.3 m, 2.4 m high): the time for the smoke layer to come down to 1.5 m with no openings, steady 180 kW from the start.
Analysis > Run Simulation with 'Open Smokeview when the run finishes' ticked: when FDS ends, Smokeview opens <CHID>.smv from the run folder (the dialog was closed here without running).
